draft.title: Purposes of civil law
card: Civil law deals with disputes between people, groups or businesses. It protects their rights, such as the right to keep a promise made in a contract or to be free from harm caused by someone else's carelessness.
When a right has been wronged, civil law aims to put the wronged party back where they were before the wrong. It usually does this by ordering the other party to pay money, called damages.
Civil law covers many areas. Negligence is careless harm. Defamation is harm to a person's reputation. Contract is a broken agreement. Nuisance is interference with the use of land.
The aim is to fix the harm to the wronged party. It is not mainly to punish the wrongdoer, which is the focus of criminal law.
draft.remember: Civil law protects rights and puts the wronged party back where they were.

a.q: What is the main purpose of an order to pay damages in a civil case?
opts: To restore the wronged party to their earlier position
To punish the wrongdoer for breaking the law
To warn the public against similar behaviour
To decide whether the wrongdoer goes to prison
a.why: Civil law aims to put the wronged party back where they were, and money is the usual way to do this. Punishing the wrongdoer is the focus of criminal law, so it is not the main purpose here.
a.clue: Think about who the civil law is trying to help.

b.q: Sam's neighbour runs a loud workshop each night, so Sam cannot use his backyard in peace. Which area of civil law does this dispute fall under?
b.why: Nuisance is interference with a person's use of their land, and the noise stops Sam enjoying his yard. Negligence is tempting, but the problem is not careless harm to a person. It is the ongoing interference with the use of land.
b.clue: Look at what the noise interferes with.

a.best: To restore the wronged party to their earlier position

problems.detail: "the right to keep a promise made in a contract" says the opposite of what is meant. The right is to have the other party keep their promise. As written, a student could misread whose right it is.
"Contract is a broken agreement" is inaccurate. A contract is a legally binding agreement; the civil wrong is a breach of contract. Better: "Contract law deals with broken agreements."
Why (b) says negligence is "careless harm to a person", which narrows the card's definition ("careless harm"). Negligence can also cover careless damage to property, so this could mislead.

check.summary: Both questions are sound, with clear single answers. The card misstates the contract right ("right to keep a promise") and calls a contract "a broken agreement", and why (b) wrongly narrows negligence to harm to a person.
